Laura / team — quick read of the MSA excerpt attached. Notes below (will follow up with marked-up PDF):

- Section 4 (data residency): we can accept language permitting EU routing for a defined pilot cohort, provided: (a) data residency guarantees remain for PHI workflows (if any), and (b) Skyline signs the pilot addendum (timeboxed, max 90 days) with explicit data handling obligations. Non-starter: open-ended territory change without addendum.
- SLA burst credits: propose to keep calculation at hourly granularity for burst pricing to avoid large rounding differences; candidate compromise: hourly for billing, daily for aggregate reporting.
- Prorated credit: ops can support one-time prorated credit; need a clean billing memo and sign-off by finance.

I'll produce a redline and attach to the order form draft by tomorrow AM. Karthik — can you draft the pilot addendum template (short, 1 page) with the metrics we need? Markus, please confirm the hourly credit calc and any rounding tolerances we should call out.

Ben Carter

Ben — draft pilot addendum attached (short checklist + trigger metrics). Summary below:

- Pilot scope: up to 500k tokens/month for EU routing; strictly non-PHI workloads.
- Duration: 90 days from go-live.
- Data handling: all logs and outputs retained in EU region; no cross-border persistence unless explicitly approved.
- Success criteria: error rate <1.5% and average p95 latency <350ms for routed requests.
- Termination: either party may end pilot with 7 days notice; production rollout requires separate commercial agreement.

Markus — suggested hourly credit calc: credit = (burst_tokens / total_hour_tokens) * hourly_charge, floor to nearest $10. Open to adjust.

I'll attach the addendum and updated order form to HubSpot and share the DocuSign link once Ben's redline is in.

Thanks,
Karthik
